problem: RGB-only end-to-end navigation policies (NoMaD, ViNT, FlowNav) fail in off-road settings with glare, shadows or night, while existing multi-modal traversability and LiDAR methods need near-perfect sensor inputs and break when a modality is degraded or missing.
motivation: Off-road environments combine extreme terrain diversity, illumination changes and frequent sensor degradation (vibration, weather, low light), so no single modality is reliable. A deployable policy should fuse RGB, thermal, LiDAR and velocity, keep working when any subset is missing, and account for the physical cost of terrain without expensive post-hoc costmap guidance.
key_idea: Fuse RGB, thermal, LiDAR pointcloud and velocity tokens with a per-modality-router sparse MoE, train with random modality dropout (mask-and-ignore), and have a diffusion policy jointly generate waypoints and an IMU-derived traversability score used to rank candidate trajectories.
insight: Ablations show the fusion backbone matters: concat fusion and a dense-transformer Modified-NoMaD have much higher collision rate (CR) and undesirable behaviors (UB) than the MoE (day CR 1.7 and 1.6 vs 0.7). Removing the traversability heuristic keeps CR relatively low but raises UB (1.9 vs 0.6), so the heuristic mainly gives terrain awareness. Modality analysis shows LiDAR drives collision avoidance while thermal and velocity improve terrain understanding, and per-modality routers plus Laplace gating beat a joint router and softmax gating.
method: Modality encoders: RGB and thermal at 96x96 via separate EfficientNet-B0 (trained from scratch); a single 48k-point LiDAR scan through PointPillars, distilled from a BEV map into a vector; ego-velocity norm via Fourier features + MLP; context of 4 observations, 256-d tokens.
Sparse MoE fusion: 4 layers, each with MHSA (4 heads) plus a sparse MoE layer with 16 experts and top-4 routing; 4 per-modality routers with Laplace gating (FuseMoE) select from a shared expert pool.

Modality dropout: per-modality Bernoulli masks drop all tokens of a modality during training (p=0.5 for RGB/LiDAR/velocity, p=0.2 for thermal); at test masks are set deterministically; no reconstruction of masked tokens (mask-and-ignore).

Traversability-augmented diffusion policy: a conditional DDPM (1-D U-Net, T=10, cosine schedule) generates 8 trajectories of 8 waypoints, each waypoint (x,y,c), where c is a self-supervised heuristic from the PSD of Z-axis IMU acceleration.
Trajectory ranking: the N sampled candidates are ranked by their predicted traversability heuristic to choose safer, smoother paths, with negligible extra compute.

Loss and planner: L = α·L_Dist (temporal distance to goal) + (1-α)β·L_Diff + (1-β)·L_MoE (load-balancing CV² loss); a topological memory serves as the high-level planner for goal-conditioned navigation.

setting.backbone: MAMMOTH: EfficientNet-B0 + PointPillars + Fourier/MLP encoders, sparse MoE fusion transformer, DDPM 1-D conditional U-Net (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: TartanDrive 2.0 plus an in-house off-road dataset (thermal LWIR, night-time), about 9 hours total; 80/20 train/test split; imitation from odometry trajectories plus IMU heuristic labels
setting.observation: RGB + thermal LWIR + Livox LiDAR pointcloud + ego velocity, with history of 4 frames, and goal image for goal-conditioned mode
setting.action_space: predicted local 2D waypoints (8 trajectories x 8 waypoints), each with a traversability value

numbers.eval_set_note: five unseen real-world off-road environments; 40 min autonomous mobility each for day and night exploration; goal navigation in daylight only
numbers.extra: trained on TartanDrive 2.0 + in-house data; CR = collisions per minute; UB = undesirable behaviors
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Comparison of E2E baselines on exploration and navigation tasks): MAMMOTH 0.7 0.6 0.8 0.75 33%

numbers.backbone: MAMMOTH without heuristic in diffusion head

numbers_note: Custom real-world metrics (CR per minute, UB counts) are not on a standard benchmark; the SR shown for MAMMOTH is a goal-reaching rate in daytime only. Missing-modality tables give CR/UB per condition (e.g., none missing day 0.7/0.6, night 0.8/0.75) and are not included above.
results: MAMMOTH gets day CR 0.7 / UB 0.6 and night CR 0.8 / UB 0.75 with 33% goal SR, while the best baseline NoMaD gets day CR 1.3 / UB 1.0 with 17% SR (a 0.6 CR reduction and 16-point SR gain). RGB-only baselines cannot operate at night, and MAMMOTH's night metrics beat all baselines' daytime metrics; it also degrades gracefully when a single modality is removed.
limitations: Goal-reaching SR is low overall (33%) because off-road scenes lack distinctive features, which degrades temporal-distance prediction; goal navigation was only tested in daylight.
Thermal data exists only in the small in-house dataset, and evaluations are short real-world runs (12-40 min) with few environments and no statistical variance reported.
Baselines were retrained by the authors and the comparison to prior traversability/costmap methods is only qualitative.
